modal:host-detach-message: This host will be detached from the pool and its local storage reset. Make sure no VMs are still running on it and that anything you need from its local storage has been backed up.
modal:host-disable-and-evacuate-vms-mess: The host will be disabled and its running VMs will be automatically migrated to other hosts in the pool, with no interruption as long as resources allow.
modal:host-disable-message: The host will be marked unavailable for starting or receiving new VMs. Already-running VMs are not affected.
modal:host-emergency-shutdown-message: This will power off the host. Its running VMs will be suspended, without migration, before the host shuts down. VMs that cannot be suspended will be shut down.
modal:host-enable-message: The host becomes available again for starting or receiving VMs.
modal:host-force-reboot-message: The host is about to reboot. Its running VMs will be migrated to other hosts when possible, but those that can't be will be forcibly shut down. Data loss may occur.

modal:host-reboot-message: The host is about to reboot. Its running VMs will be migrated to other hosts and won't be moved back to it automatically afterwards.
modal:host-restart-toolstack-message: The host's management service (toolstack) is about to restart. Running VMs won't be interrupted, but they'll be temporarily unmanageable (a few minutes).
modal:host-shutdown-message: This will power off the host. Any VMs still running on it will be migrated to another running host.
modal:host-smart-reboot-message: All running VMs on this host will be suspended, the host will reboot, then the VMs will automatically resume. This causes temporary downtime. If Xen Orchestra itself runs on this host, VMs may not resume automatically.

what-does-protected-mean-content: A VM is considered protected when it’s included in at least one scheduled backup job and the last three runs of that job completed successfully. This helps ensure the VM has recent, reliable recovery points.
what-is-a-disabled-host-content: A disabled host is a running host on which no new VM can be started. VMs already running on it keep running.
what-is-an-eol-host-content: An EOL (End of Life) host is a server running a version of Xen or an operating system that is no longer supported by its vendor. It no longer receives updates, bug fixes or security patches, which can make it unstable or vulnerable. We recommend upgrading to a supported version to ensure performance, compatibility and security.
what-is-an-unreachable-pool-content: A pool is considered unreachable when Xen Orchestra can no longer communicate with it. This may happen if the pool is offline, the network is misconfigured, or credentials have changed.
what-is-an-unreachable-pool-tip: To restore access, verify the pool is running, check your connection, and ensure credentials are up to date.
